findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only declaration, in `UsernamePasswordForm` (line 160), takes a `UserModel` parameter, and no no-arg overload exists in the class hierarchy. The `services` module will not compile. The call should pass the user, e.g. `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`.

findings.title: `user != null` turns off conditional passkeys for normal (unidentified) login
findings.body:
`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. Before this change, webauthn data was filled exactly when no user was selected (`context.getUser() == null`). The new check does the opposite: on a first login there is no context user, so `authenticate()` (line 115) never calls `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm`. Passkey conditional UI and the discoverable-key auto login therefore no longer appear on the initial login page.

The error path is affected too. `getUser()` calls `context.clearUser()`, and `validateUser` only sets the user after the password is validated. So `challenge(context, error, field)` (line 137) also sees a null user after an invalid username or invalid password, and passkeys vanish from the error page.

This breaks the main passkeys feature; existing tests such as `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey` should fail. The check should allow `user == null` (for example `user == null || <user has passkey credential>`) rather than require a non-null user.

findings.title: Re-authentication enables passkeys for any identified user, even one with no passkey credential
findings.body:
For an already-identified user, the new condition depends only on the realm setting. It never checks whether that user has a passwordless/passkey credential (e.g. `user.credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(webauthnAuth.getCredentialType())`). Two problems follow:

1. During re-authentication (e.g. `prompt=login`), users without passkeys are shown the passkey UI and a browser WebAuthn prompt they cannot complete.
2. In `UsernameForm.authenticate`, the shortcut that skips the username step for an already-identified user is disabled whenever the realm has passkeys enabled. Every re-authenticating user, including those without passkeys, gets an extra username form with the username hidden and nothing to fill in.

The condition should also require that the current user actually has a passkey credential.

findings.title: "User without passkey" test actually disables passkeys for the whole realm
findings.body:
`reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` and its comment claim to check that passkeys are not shown during re-authentication "as this user does not have passkey". The test, however, sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`, which turns the feature off realm-wide.

The case that matters is not covered: a realm with passkeys enabled and a user who has no passkey credential re-authenticating. That is exactly where the new `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` logic misbehaves, showing the passkey UI and no longer skipping `UsernameForm`. The test should keep passkeys enabled and log in as a user without a WebAuthn credential.
